title: Include a surprising extreme case

variants.label: さえ · even this case

segments.role: さえ selects the teacher as a striking case: if even this knowledgeable person could not answer, the difficulty is remarkable. さえ does not always require a negative predicate, and this is not the sufficient-condition construction さえ〜ば.

example.translation: Even the teacher could not answer this difficult question.
example.note: You expected the teacher to manage a question the learners found difficult.

variants.change: さえ selects the teacher as a striking case: if even this knowledgeable person could not answer, the difficulty is remarkable. さえ does not always require a negative predicate, and this is not the sufficient-condition construction さえ〜ば.

variants.label: まで · extends even to

segments.role: Inclusion まで extends the scope even to the teacher, beyond the people you would normally expect. Both variants work in this scene; there is no universal stronger-or-weaker ranking. This is an additional “even” use of まで, distinct from an endpoint such as 五時まで and from an extreme measure such as 借りてまで.

example.translation: Even the teacher could not answer this difficult question.
example.note: The group unable to answer extends unexpectedly to the teacher as well.

question: What does 先生まで答えられなかった add in this scene?
answers: The people unable to answer include even the teacher, unexpectedly.
The teacher had until a stated deadline to answer.
The teacher answered only after all the learners had answered.
feedback: まで includes the teacher as an unexpected extension of the group. It does not set a deadline here. さえ also highlights the surprising teacher case, but foregrounds it as a telling extreme example.
